# Aunt Lavinia

deceased

## Overview

- **Age:** at least seventy  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P54](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0054)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P58](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0058), [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Lavinia is a slender, stern, and unbending woman. Her eyes flash behind a pair of gold-rimmed spectacles.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P77](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0077)_

## Personality

Aunt Lavinia is known for a bad temper and an exceedingly strict, proper demeanor that often leads to severe scolding. However, towards specific individuals, she has shown a contrasting, gentle side.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P54](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0054), [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P58](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0058), [v3 ch.Nell-girl P29](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0029)_

## History

Aunt Lavinia was a wealthy, elderly resident of [Port Marlow](../codex/places.md#port-marlow) and the aunt of Isolde's father. During a visit to the [Pembroke](../character/pembroke.md) home, she was infuriated after [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and Isolde inadvertently jumped onto her in bed late at night; however, when [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) took full responsibility and apologized, Aunt Lavinia was won over by her honesty, forgave Isolde, and formed a fond friendship with [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md). She later invited [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and Isolde to stay at her home, [Beechwood](../codex/places.md#beechwood), where she welcomed them warmly for a week of town attractions, including the [Exhibition](../codex/places.md#exhibition) and a concert.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P9](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0009), [v1 CHAPTER XIX. ## Quotes

> "Oh, is that so, hey? It seems to me Isolde performed at least her fair portion of the leaping. Such behavior occurring within an honorable home!"
>
> — Aunt Lavinia — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P82](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0082)

> “My decision is made to remain merely to become more familiar with that Nell-girl,” she admitted openly. “She entertains me, and when one reaches my age, somebody who provides entertainment is uncommon.”
>
> — Aunt Lavinia — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P92](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0092)

> "Bear in mind, you Nell-girl, that you are to pay me a visit when you arrive in town, where I will lodge you in the most unoccupied spare-room bed I have for sleeping."
>
> — Aunt Lavinia — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P96](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0096)

> "Goodness, child, what growth you’ve had! I do declare, you stand taller than me. Furthermore, you are far better-looking than you used to be as well. Though I expect you are already aware of that without anyone telling you."
>
> — Aunt Lavinia — [v1 CHAPTER XXIX. An Epoch in Nell’s Life P18](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0018)

> "I suppose I might if you drop by to chat with me every now and then,"
>
> — Aunt Lavinia — [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P90](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0090)

## Relationships

### [Isolde Pembroke](../character/isolde-pembroke.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/aunt-lavinia--isolde-pembroke.md)

Aunt Lavinia is the aunt of [Isolde Pembroke](../character/isolde-pembroke.md). Isolde assists [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) in capturing a garden conversation while they wait in a duckhouse, after which they purchase a willow-ware platter together and drive away along [Tory Road](../codex/places.md#tory-road).

### [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/aunt-lavinia--nell-harcourt.md)

Aunt Lavinia and [Nell Harcourt](../character/nell-harcourt.md) share a fond friendship that begins after an initial misadventure. When [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and Isolde accidentally jump onto Aunt Lavinia in bed late at night, Aunt Lavinia is initially furious and threatens to leave; however, [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) takes full responsibility and apologizes directly, winning over the strict woman with her charm and honesty. Aunt Lavinia subsequently invites [Nell](../character/nell-harcourt.md) and Isolde to stay at her town home, [Beechwood](../codex/places.md#beechwood), where she warmly hosts them for a week of local attractions and concerts.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XIX. A Concert, a Catastrophe, and a Confession P9](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0009), [v1 CHAPTER XIX.
